title: My apartment in Uralsk
paragraphs: My name is Kamila Dzhaksybekova. I am 18 years old and I am from Kokshetau. I study Economics at WKU. Unlike most of my classmates, I do not live in the student dormitory. I rent a small apartment near the university with my friend Zara from our group. Our apartment is on the third floor of a quiet residential building, just a ten-minute walk from the WKU campus. It is not big, but it is our home — and we love it!

There is a small hallway when you first enter the apartment. In the hallway, there is a large mirror on the wall and there are two coat hooks for our jackets and bags. There is also a shoe rack near the door. The hallway leads to three rooms: the living room, the bedroom, and the kitchen. There is one bathroom at the end of the short corridor.

The living room is the biggest room in our apartment. There is a comfortable blue sofa against the wall — big enough for two people to sit and watch films together. There is a small wooden coffee table in front of the sofa. On the wall, there is a flat-screen television. There are two bookshelves near the window — one is Kamila's with Economics textbooks, and the other is Zara's with novels and poetry books. There is a large window with white curtains that lets in beautiful morning light.

The kitchen is small but very practical. There is a round table in the centre with four chairs around it. This is where Zara and I have breakfast and dinner together every day. There is a fridge in the corner — it is always full of vegetables, fruit, and yoghurt. There is a microwave above the counter and a small electric kettle for making tea. There is also a washing machine under the counter, which is very convenient for students.

Zara and I share one bedroom. There are two single beds on opposite sides of the room. There is a large wardrobe between the beds where we keep our clothes. There is a study desk near the window for Zara, and there is a small desk in the corner for me. There is a reading lamp on each desk. There are two small bedside tables next to the beds — mine has a book and a phone charger on it, and Zara's has a small cactus plant!

The bathroom is very small — there is only room for a sink, a shower, and a small shelf. There is a mirror above the sink and there are some toiletries on the shelf: shampoo, soap, and toothbrushes. There is no bathtub — only a shower. But the water is always hot, which is the most important thing! There are some hooks on the door for our towels.

My favourite feature of the apartment is the balcony. There is a small balcony off the living room with a view of the quiet street below and the trees in the courtyard. There are four potted plants on the balcony — Zara brought them from home and she waters them every morning. In the summer, we sometimes drink tea on the balcony in the evenings and talk about our day.

Our apartment costs 80,000 tenge per month — we each pay 40,000. This is more expensive than the dormitory, but we have more freedom and more space. There are no noisy neighbours in our building and there is a small park just around the corner. I feel very lucky to have such a nice apartment with such a good friend. As my mother says: "A good home makes a good student!" I completely agree.

dialogue.speaker: Zara
dialogue.text: Kamila! Your cousin is here — she wants to see our apartment!

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Great! Come in! There is a coat hook here for your jacket.

dialogue.speaker: Zara
dialogue.text: Wow — it's bigger than I imagined! Is there a living room?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Yes! There is a sofa, a TV, and look — there are two bookshelves!

dialogue.speaker: Zara
dialogue.text: And there is a big window! Is there a nice view?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Just the courtyard — but there are some beautiful trees. Very peaceful.

dialogue.speaker: Zara
dialogue.text: What about the kitchen? Is there a dishwasher?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Ha! No, there isn't a dishwasher. But there is a washing machine!

dialogue.speaker: Zara
dialogue.text: That's great! Are there two beds in the bedroom?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Yes, there are two beds and a big wardrobe. And there is a desk for each of us.

dialogue.speaker: Zara
dialogue.text: Is there a balcony? I saw a window outside that looked like one.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Yes! There are plants on it and a lovely view. Let's have tea there!
